title: Concealment
catches: Hiding facts, keeping them out of writing, destroying records, or moving a conversation to a channel that is not retained.
does_not_prove: That anything was hidden. Confidentiality is routine, and secrecy words fill email disclaimers.

title: Accounting manipulation
catches: Earnings management, off-ledger entries, and false, backdated or disguised records.
does_not_prove: A misstatement. Several of these phrases are also ordinary accounting vocabulary.

title: Bribery and corruption
catches: Euphemisms for improper payments, fees that disguise them, avoided controls, and collusion on tenders and prices.
does_not_prove: That a payment was made, or that it was improper.

title: Pressure, rationalisation and dissent
catches: The human side of the fraud triangle: pressure to perform, financial distress, excuses, and the unease or objection of people asked to take part.
does_not_prove: Wrongdoing. The writer may be the person refusing it.

title: Hostility and intimidation
catches: Profanity, insults, smears and intimidation that stops short of a physical threat.
does_not_prove: A conflict of any legal significance.

title: Legal exposure
catches: Investigations, lawsuits, prosecution, regulators' actions and the preservation of documents.
does_not_prove: That the writer is involved. Lawyers, compliance staff and journalists write these words.

title: Crime
catches: Labels of illegality and the names of common offences.
does_not_prove: That an offence took place. These are mostly the words of accusers, reporters and policies.

title: Financial crime
catches: Money laundering, sanctions and export-control evasion, market manipulation, insider dealing, tax fraud and embezzlement.
does_not_prove: That an offence took place. Compliance training and policies use the same words.

title: Violence and terrorism
catches: Physical threats, weapons, attacks and violent extremism.
does_not_prove: A threat. News, fiction and figures of speech use the same words.

title: Sexual misconduct and exploitation
catches: Harassment, assault, grooming and trafficking indicators, in the published legal and financial-intelligence vocabulary.
does_not_prove: That misconduct occurred.

title: Coded language
catches: Oblique references and documented code words from trading chat rooms and drug-trade slang.
does_not_prove: Anything on its own. Most of these are everyday words and count only beside other signals.

title: Scam
catches: Advance-fee, lottery, investment, romance and impersonation scripts.
does_not_prove: That anyone was defrauded, or who wrote the script.

title: Marketing and bulk mail
catches: Unsubscribe footers, offers and newsletter furniture.
does_not_prove: What kind of document this is. Transactional mail carries some of the same furniture.

title: Legal register
catches: The drafting vocabulary of legal instruments, pleadings and sworn statements.
does_not_prove: What kind of document this is. The vocabulary is quoted and discussed as often as it is used.

title: Contract
catches: Clause headings and the operative language of contracts.
does_not_prove: That a contract exists or was signed.

title: Legal letter
catches: Letters before action, demands, formal notices and correspondence between lawyers.
does_not_prove: What kind of document this is. The vocabulary is quoted and discussed as often as it is used.

title: Memorandum of understanding
catches: Memoranda of understanding, letters of intent, heads of terms and other instruments that state intent without binding.
does_not_prove: That an agreement was reached.

title: Invoice
catches: Invoice fields and invoice types.
does_not_prove: That a document is an invoice. Orders, statements and quotations share the fields.

title: Draft or superseded invoice
catches: Pro forma, draft, corrected and partial invoices, and quotations.
does_not_prove: Which version is final.

title: Final invoice
catches: Final and settled invoices, and receipts.
does_not_prove: That payment was made.

title: Proof of payment
catches: Payment confirmations, remittance advices, and the fields of SWIFT MT103 and ISO 20022 payment messages.
does_not_prove: That money moved. Payment screenshots and message copies are easy to forge.

title: International transfer
catches: Correspondent and intermediary banking, cross-border charges and purpose codes, money transfer operators and hawala.
does_not_prove: That a transfer crossed a border. The validated IBAN and BIC entities are the stronger evidence.

title: Jurisdiction
catches: Governing-law and forum clauses, courts, arbitral institutions, statutes and offshore centres.
does_not_prove: Which law applies. A document names many places it is not governed by.
